claims.statement: The named local schedules preserve fixed-generation reader rights across publication and authority restart under both drain and pinned-generation policies.
The local stable-range lock excludes a second cooperating authority; restarted or revoked publisher permits refuse selection changes in the named schedules.
Named local reclamation cuts resume from durable retirement intent, retain pinned bytes and permit old-generation deletion while a current-generation reader remains active.
Seventy-five finite abstract fixtures expose selected cross-arm shortcuts while permitting guarded examples; they establish neither upstream runtime behavior nor implementation correctness.
